note: Awakening sets letting-be against objectifying fixing-in-place; we shall not speak of ascertaining but of awakening.
Awakening = making something wakeful, letting whatever is sleeping become wakeful.
Waking and sleeping are not equivalent to consciousness and unconsciousness (dreaming pertains to sleep).
Making an attunement an object of knowledge achieves the contrary of awakening: it is destroyed, weakened, altered.
De Somno: sleep characterized as akinesia, not via (un)consciousness.
Sleep as a being-bound, a peculiar way in which aisthesis is bound.
The binding reaches perception and our essence, unable to take in other beings.
Antiquity grasped sleep more elementarily than modern misinterpretations.
The being of man named being-there, in distinction to the being-at-hand of the stone.
Being-away is itself a way of man's being, not non-being.
Man must be there in order to be able to be away; all being-away presupposes being-there.
The there-and-not-there of attunement has to do with the innermost essence of man's being, his Dasein.
Faced with attunement as a way of being-with, we must dismiss the psychology of feelings, experiences, and consciousness.
Attunement is the way of our being-there with one another; neither inside nor outside, it imposes itself on everything.
The fundamental way in which Dasein is as Dasein, giving Dasein subsistence and possibility.
Weise = way/manner but also melody/tune; attunement sets the tone for and determines man's being.
The least-noticed attunements are the most powerful; Dasein is always already attuned; there is only ever a change of attunement.
Awakening attunement = grasping Da-sein as Da-sein, or letting Da-sein be as it can be; since awakening is an acting, we must act in accordance with it.
Decline of the West: decline of life in and through spirit (ratio).
Spirit as the adversary of the soul, a sickness to be exorcised to liberate life.
Man in the epoch of balance between life and spirit.
A mediating epoch, a new Middle Ages sublating the life/spirit opposition; least original of the four.
Dionysian = urge for unity, reaching beyond the person; Apollonian = urge for complete being-for-oneself, freedom under the law.
All four diagnoses point back to Nietzsche as their common source; life/spirit is the residual literary form of Dionysos/Apollo.
Culture-diagnosis releases us from ourselves, imparting a world-historical role; it sets out man (Dar-stellung) but never his Da-sein.
Foreign words chosen deliberately to mark the non-binding, sensational, literary character of culture-philosophy.
Behind our need for a role and the indifference yawning from all things lies a concealed profound boredom.
FIRST naming: profound boredom draws back and forth like a silent fog in the abysses of Dasein.
Profound boredom posed as the sought-after fundamental attunement that must be awakened.
We find ourselves not via culture-diagnosis but by binding ourselves to our Da-sein, given over to becoming what we are.
Concealed-yet-pervasive boredom under occupied surface grounds the surface/depth split of the EEG-vs-gaze contradiction.
Least-noticed-most-powerful attunement underwrites the bored subject's restless looking-around to find something to attend to (high gaze-variance).
Ascertaining a present-at-hand correlate is not awakening the attunement; a contradictory EEG/gaze reading is predicted, not a measurement failure.
